newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Japanese rates set for economy, not banks - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Japanese rates set for economy, not banks - BOJ.

text.p: Japanese interest rates were not low to help the banking sector overcome its problems with bad loans, but were designed to support the real economy, an adviser to the Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor said on Monday.

"The aim of this, you might call it low interest rate policy, is to support the real economy rather than banks," Kengo Inoue, research and statistics adivisor to the BOJ Governor, told reporters when asked if short term rates were providing support to banks for loan write offs.
Inoue had earlier delivered a speech to a business conference on the Japanese banking sector.

Banks had an opportunity to improve profits when rates were being eased, because as loans matured less rapidly then deposits, lending interest rates came down slower than deposit interest rates, but when rates stabilized it did not help banks that much, he said.
"Interest rate policy is a macro-economic tool rather than a prudential tool, and we make that distinction very clear," Inoue said.
He also was asked about the use of public funds to purchase land assets of troubled financial firms, an idea that had been raised in February.
There had been a move, particularly for local authorities, to expedite some of the plans to buy up land, but Inoue said there was no concrete plan by the government.
He said it was unlikely that there would be a large scale buy-out, but individual authorities might try to.
"I wish to add, that the government never said that, the idea was floated by politicians, but the government never said it would do that," Inoue said
